speaker: josias_thwaite
text: Brethren, he entered the city, and they cried before him. Consider who cry Hosanna on the Sunday.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: I am not looking at you while I say it. A crowd is a wind. It turns. The same mouths can learn another word before Friday.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: There have been no palms in this church these thirty years. I will not dress a lesson in green wood to make it kinder.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Thirty years. He has said the number, and he has looked at nobody. That is the whole of his courtesy this morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not writing it down.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The Mayor's pew is full, sir. Sir John is in it. He has not been looked at either.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then we are even with the pew. I am in the south aisle, and I have a king in my head who rides in behind another man.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Keep your king out of my pew. This is a parish, not a page. The wind is raw. Sit in it.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: Dust on a man's head is a sermon the street already knows. I am not giving you a second city. I am giving you this one, and the mouths in it.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: Who cry Hosanna on the Sunday may be quiet by the week's end. I do not ask their names. I ask you to hear the turn.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I hear it. I am not putting a pen to it. Holinshed has a king who comes in behind another man, and dust thrown on his head. That is mine. It can wait until I am out of your aisle.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Good. Wait. I did not bring you here to furnish a book.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: There is no palm to hold. I looked along the ledge. Bare stone, and the wind.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: Bare is the lesson. A branch would flatter you. I will not flatter a parish that can change its cry between two bells.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not flatter it either. I have written nothing. I mean to leave with nothing written.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then sit. The south aisle is where this house sits, and you are of the house this morning.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Sir John has his hand on the pew door and has not opened his mouth. I am only saying what I see.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: The lesson is the fickleness of crowds. Remember that, and do not remember me as a man who picked a face out of you.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will remember the wind. It is an east wind, and it is raw. The rest can stay in the air until I am home.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Home is for the almanac. You will not make a note on your knee in my parish.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No note. No knee. I am thinking of dust, and I am not writing dust.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: Go on hearing, those who have ears. I have more to say, and I shall not spend it on a glance.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: He means it. He has not found a face yet.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Let him not find mine. I am tired, and the king can wait in the cold with me.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Tired is allowed. A page is not. We will go when he lets the parish go, and not before.
